claim: Microdeletions and microduplications of the 16p11.2 chromosomal locus are associated with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders.
source: Microdeletions and microduplications of the 16p11.2 chromosomal locus are associated with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders and reciprocal physiological conditions such as macro/microcephaly and high/low body mass index.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known association in the literature.

claim: 16p11.2 CNVs are associated with reciprocal physiological conditions such as macro/microcephaly and high/low body mass index.
source: Microdeletions and microduplications of the 16p11.2 chromosomal locus are associated with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders and reciprocal physiological conditions such as macro/microcephaly and high/low body mass index.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known association.

claim: 65 clones of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) were generated from 13 individuals with 16p11.2 copy number variations (CNVs).
source: To facilitate cellular and molecular investigations into these phenotypes, 65 clones of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) were generated from 13 individuals with 16p11.2 copy number variations (CNVs).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental work performed in the study.

claim: A customizable bioinformatic strategy for the detection of random integration and expression of reprogramming vectors was developed.
source: To ensure these cell lines were suitable for downstream mechanistic investigations, a customizable bioinformatic strategy for the detection of random integration and expression of reprogramming vectors was developed and leveraged towards identifying a subset of 'footprint'-free hiPSC clones.
evidence: This describes a methodological development reported in the study.

claim: Transcriptomic profiling of cortical neural progenitor cells derived from these hiPSCs identified alterations in gene expression patterns which precede morphological abnormalities reported at later neurodevelopmental stages.
source: Transcriptomic profiling of cortical neural progenitor cells derived from these hiPSCs identified alterations in gene expression patterns which precede morphological abnormalities reported at later neurodevelopmental stages.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the transcriptomic analysis performed in the study.

claim: Transcriptional data revealed disruptions in gene programs related to both nervous system function and cellular metabolism.
source: Interpreting clinical information—available with the cell lines by request from the Simons Foundation Autism Research Initiative—with this transcriptional data revealed disruptions in gene programs related to both nervous system function and cellular metabolism.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of transcriptional data in the context of clinical information.

claim: CNVs play a role in the etiology of various neuropsychiatric disorders including intellectual disability.
source: Copy number variations (CNVs) play a role in the etiology of various neuropsychiatric disorders including intellectual disability (Malhotra and Sebat, 2012), developmental delay (Malhotra and Sebat, 2012), congenital malformations (Cooper et al., 2011), autism spectrum disorder (ASD) (Sebat et al., 2007; Pinto et al., 2010), schizophrenia (SCZ) (Walsh et al., 2008; Levinson et al., 2011), bipolar disorder (BD) (Rucker et al., 2013), and recurrent depression (Malhotra et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Microdeletions and microduplications of a 593 kb region of chromosome 16p11.2 have been implicated as a penetrant risk factor in the onset of neurodevelopmental disorders including ASD and SCZ.
source: Microdeletions and microduplications of a 593 kb region of chromosome 16p11.2 have been implicated as a penetrant risk factor in the onset of neurodevelopmental disorders including ASD and SCZ (Weiss et al., 2008; McCarthy et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The 16p11.2 chromosomal region spans 29.4–32.2 Mb in the reference genome (GRCh37/hg19) and encompasses 29 genes, of which 25 are protein coding.
source: This chromosomal region spans 29.4–32.2 Mb in the reference genome (GRCh37/hg19) and encompasses 29 genes, of which 25 are protein coding (Weiss et al., 2008; Jacquemont et al., 2011; Blumenthal et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a genomic characterization supported by citations.

claim: The presence of a deletion or duplication at the 16p11.2 chromosomal locus is found in approximately 1% of individuals with ASD.
source: While estimates of prevalence vary, multiple studies report the presence of a deletion or duplication at the 16p11.2 chromosomal locus in approximately 1% of individuals with ASD (Sebat et al., 2007; Weiss et al., 2008; Jacquemont et al., 2011; Stefansson et al., 2014) and between 0.01% and 0.1% of the general population (Weiss et al., 2008; Jacquemont et al., 2011; Stefansson et al., 2014).
evidence: This prevalence estimate is supported by multiple citations.

claim: 16p11.2 CNVs are found in between 0.01% and 0.1% of the general population.
source: While estimates of prevalence vary, multiple studies report the presence of a deletion or duplication at the 16p11.2 chromosomal locus in approximately 1% of individuals with ASD (Sebat et al., 2007; Weiss et al., 2008; Jacquemont et al., 2011; Stefansson et al., 2014) and between 0.01% and 0.1% of the general population (Weiss et al., 2008; Jacquemont et al., 2011; Stefansson et al., 2014).
evidence: This prevalence estimate is supported by multiple citations.

claim: A meta-analysis of seven studies suggests an overall prevalence of 0.76% 16p11.2 CNVs among idiopathic ASD probands.
source: A meta-analysis of seven studies suggests an overall prevalence of 0.76% 16p11.2 CNVs among idiopathic ASD probands (Walsh and Bracken, 2011).
evidence: This is a specific prevalence estimate from a cited meta-analysis.

claim: Both microdeletions and microduplications of 16p11.2 are associated with ASD, although ASD represents a greater proportion of the diagnoses associated with 16p11.2 deletion.
source: Both microdeletions and microduplications of 16p11.2 are associated with ASD, although ASD represents a greater proportion of the diagnoses associated with 16p11.2 deletion (Walsh and Bracken, 2011; Glessner et al., 2009; Shen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The risk of SCZ is greater in 16p11.2 microduplication carriers.
source: Conversely, the risk of SCZ is greater in 16p11.2 microduplication carriers (Walsh et al., 2008; McCarthy et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Individuals with a microdeletion of the 16p11.2 locus present with macrocephaly, increased overall gray and white matter volumes, increased cortical surface area, and increased axial diffusivity of white matter tracts.
source: Specifically, individuals with a microdeletion of the 16p11.2 locus present with macrocephaly, increased overall gray and white matter volumes, increased cortical surface area, and increased axial diffusivity of white matter tracts such as the anterior corpus callosum and the internal and external capsules (Shinawi et al., 2010; Qureshi et al., 2014; Owen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a phenotypic description supported by citations.

claim: Individuals with a microduplication of 16p11.2 present with microcephaly and corresponding decreases in gray matter, white matter, and cortical surface area.
source: Individuals with a microduplication of 16p11.2 present with microcephaly and corresponding decreases in gray matter, white matter, and cortical surface area (Shinawi et al., 2010; Qureshi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a phenotypic description supported by citations.

claim: Recent studies have characterized independent and reciprocal abnormalities in both auditory processing delays and the amplitude of visual evoked potentials among individuals with the 16p11.2 CNVs.
source: Recent studies have characterized independent and reciprocal abnormalities in both auditory processing delays and the amplitude of visual evoked potentials among individuals with the 16p11.2 CNVs (Jenkins et al., 2016; LeBlanc and Nelson, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Obesity and hyperphagia are observed among deletion carriers, while low body mass index (BMI) is observed in duplication carriers.
source: Finally, obesity and hyperphagia are observed among deletion carriers, while low body mass index (BMI) is observed in duplication carriers (Jacquemont et al., 2011; Walters et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a phenotypic observation supported by citations.

claim: Human somatic cells can be reprogrammed into human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) which can be differentiated into ectodermal, endodermal, and mesodermal derivatives.
source: Investigators probing the etiology of neurodevelopmental disorders acquired a powerful new tool with the discovery that human somatic cells can be reprogrammed into human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) which, in turn, can be differentiated into ectodermal, endodermal, and mesodermal derivatives (Takahashi et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a well-established scientific fact supported by citations.

claim: hiPSC-mediated neurodevelopmental disease modeling is hampered by intra- and inter-patient variability.
source: In the years that followed, the field of hiPSC-mediated neurodevelopmental disease modeling, while hampered by intra- and inter-patient variability (Brennand et al., 2012), has capitalized on the medium's unique ability to provide: (1) a model of human development at pathologically-relevant time points, (2) an unlimited source of cells for examination, and (3) tissue-specific cell types which share the genetic background of the somatic cell donor.
evidence: This is a known limitation in the field supported by a citation.

claim: Neurons derived from 16p11.2 patient hiPSCs exhibit abnormal somatic size and dendritic morphology.
source: Previous work has shown that neurons derived from 16p11.2 patient hiPSCs exhibit abnormal somatic size and dendritic morphology (Deshpande et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a finding from prior research supported by a citation.

claim: Transcriptional and phenotypic abnormalities have been observed in hiPSC-derived cortical neural stem cells derived from individuals with idiopathic ASD.
source: Interestingly, transcriptional and phenotypic abnormalities have also been observed in hiPSC-derived cortical neural stem cells derived from individuals with idiopathic ASD (Marchetto et al., 2017; Schafer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The 16p11.2 deletion has widespread effects on signaling pathways that underpin critical neural progenitor functions, including proliferation and fate choice.
source: The 16p11.2 deletion has widespread effects on signaling pathways that underpin critical neural progenitor functions, including proliferation and fate choice (Pucilowska et al., 2018), yet 16p11.2 CNV-related alterations in gene expression patterns have not been examined in early neuroepithelial precursors (radial glia), the stem and progenitor cells of the developing cortex.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: 16p11.2 CNV-related alterations in gene expression patterns have not been examined in early neuroepithelial precursors (radial glia).
source: The 16p11.2 deletion has widespread effects on signaling pathways that underpin critical neural progenitor functions, including proliferation and fate choice (Pucilowska et al., 2018), yet 16p11.2 CNV-related alterations in gene expression patterns have not been examined in early neuroepithelial precursors (radial glia), the stem and progenitor cells of the developing cortex.
evidence: This identifies a gap in the literature that the current study addresses.

claim: 65 hiPSC clones were generated from 13 donors, with ten donors harboring a microdeletion at the 16p11.2 chromosomal locus and three donors carrying a microduplication.
source: In total, 65 hiPSC clones were generated from 13 donors. Ten donors harbor a microdeletion at the 16p11.2 chromosomal locus and three donors carry a microduplication.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental work performed.

claim: All hiPSC lines reported are available through the Simons Foundation Autism Research Initiative (SFARI).
source: All lines reported here are available through the Simons Foundation Autism Research Initiative (SFARI) (https://sfari.org/resources/autism-models/ips-cells).
evidence: This is a statement about resource availability.

claim: A relatively high frequency of hiPSC clones were found to contain randomly integrated reprogramming vectors, despite the use of non-integrating episomal reprogramming strategies.
source: As a cautionary note, we also report on the relatively high frequency at which hiPSC clones were found to contain randomly integrated reprogramming vectors, in spite of the use of non-integrating episomal reprogramming strategies.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's quality control analysis.

claim: Cryptic reprogramming vector integration led to inappropriate expression of reprogramming genes in neural progenitor cells (NPCs).
source: In many clones, this led to the inappropriate expression of reprogramming genes in neural progenitor cells (NPCs), which had a more penetrant impact on genome-wide gene expression patterns than the 16p11.2 CNVs.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of integration effects.

claim: Inappropriate expression of reprogramming genes in NPCs had a more penetrant impact on genome-wide gene expression patterns than the 16p11.2 CNVs.
source: In many clones, this led to the inappropriate expression of reprogramming genes in neural progenitor cells (NPCs), which had a more penetrant impact on genome-wide gene expression patterns than the 16p11.2 CNVs.
evidence: This is a comparative finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Only a subset of genes within the 16p11.2 CNV locus are expressed in early NPCs.
source: Moreover, we report that only a subset of genes within the 16p11.2 CNV locus are expressed in early NPCs, and 14 of these genes show significant reduction in RNA abundance in clones that carry the 16p11.2 deletion.
evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 14 genes within the 16p11.2 CNV locus show significant reduction in RNA abundance in clones that carry the 16p11.2 deletion.
source: Moreover, we report that only a subset of genes within the 16p11.2 CNV locus are expressed in early NPCs, and 14 of these genes show significant reduction in RNA abundance in clones that carry the 16p11.2 deletion.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Alterations in 16p11.2 region gene expression are accompanied by changes in the expression of 93 additional genes that are not located within the 16p11.2 deletion interval.
source: We also show that these alterations are accompanied by changes in the expression of 93 additional genes that are not located within the 16p11.2 deletion interval, including genes with known relevance in neurodevelopment.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: The 93 differentially expressed genes outside the 16p11.2 interval include genes with known relevance in neurodevelopment.
source: We also show that these alterations are accompanied by changes in the expression of 93 additional genes that are not located within the 16p11.2 deletion interval, including genes with known relevance in neurodevelopment.
evidence: This is a characterization of the differentially expressed genes.

claim: Differentially expressed genes impinge on signaling pathways relevant to recently described phenotypic abnormalities in neurons in vitro and in human carriers in vivo.
source: These genes impinge on signaling pathways relevant to recently described phenotypic abnormalities in neurons in vitro (Deshpande et al., 2017) and in human carriers in vivo (Shinawi et al., 2010; Qureshi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differentially expressed genes in the context of prior research.

claim: Correlation analysis between gene networks and clinical traits from donors identified cellular metabolism as a compelling avenue for continued investigation.
source: Finally, we expand upon these findings by exploring the correlation between gene networks and clinical traits from donors and identify cellular metabolism as a compelling avenue for continued investigation.
evidence: This is a finding from the WGCNA analysis.

claim: Within the cohort of ten deletion donors, there are seven males and three females ranging in age from 6 to 41 years (mean 13.8 ± 9.98 years).
source: Within the cohort of ten deletion donors, there are seven males and three females ranging in age from 6 to 41 years (mean 13.8 ± 9.98 years) [Figure 1B].
evidence: This is demographic information about the study cohort, also shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Seven of the ten deletion donors are probands, one is the father of a proband, and two are siblings of a proband.
source: Seven of the ten donors are probands, one is the father of a proband, and two are siblings of a proband.
evidence: This is demographic information about the study cohort.

claim: Four deletion donors carry de novo mutations, and one carries an inherited mutation.
source: It is known that four donors carry de novo mutations, and one carries an inherited mutation.
evidence: This is genetic information about the study cohort.

claim: Of the three duplication donors, two are female and one is male with ages ranging from 5 to 38 years (23.33 ± 16.80 years).
source: Of the three duplication donors, two are female and one is male with ages ranging from 5 to 38 years (23.33 ± 16.80 years).
evidence: This is demographic information about the study cohort.

claim: Among the three duplication donors, one is a proband and the other two are a mother (of the aforementioned proband) and a father of a proband from whom hiPSCs were not derived.
source: Among the three duplication donors, one is a proband and the other two are a mother (of the aforementioned proband) and a father of a proband from whom hiPSCs were not derived.
evidence: This is demographic information about the study cohort.

claim: Of the three duplication donors, one carries a de novo mutation and one carries an inherited mutation.
source: Of the three donors, one carries a de novo mutation and one carries an inherited mutation.
evidence: This is genetic information about the study cohort.

claim: Among the 16p11.2 deletion donors, the most common diagnosis was articulation disorder (7 of 10 individuals).
source: Among the 16p11.2 deletion donors, the most common diagnosis was articulation disorder (7 of 10 individuals), followed by ASD (4 of 10), an IQ below 70 (4 of 10), language disorder (4 of 10), and coordination disorder (4 of 10) [Figure 1C].
evidence: This is clinical information about the study cohort, also shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Among the 16p11.2 deletion donors, 4 of 10 were diagnosed with ASD.
source: Among the 16p11.2 deletion donors, the most common diagnosis was articulation disorder (7 of 10 individuals), followed by ASD (4 of 10), an IQ below 70 (4 of 10), language disorder (4 of 10), and coordination disorder (4 of 10) [Figure 1C].
evidence: This is clinical information about the study cohort, also shown in Figure 1C.

claim: None of the 16p11.2 duplication donors were diagnosed with ASD or SCZ.
source: None of the 16p11.2 duplication donors were diagnosed with ASD or SCZ, although one individual has articulation disorder while another has mood disorder [Figure 1C].
evidence: This is clinical information about the study cohort, also shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Skin fibroblasts from each 16p11.2 CNV donor were transformed with episomal reprogramming vectors that express SOX2, OCT3/4, KLF4, LIN28, L-MYC, and P53-shRNA.
source: Skin fibroblasts from each 16p11.2 CNV donor were transformed with episomal reprogramming vectors that express SOX2, OCT3/4, KLF4, LIN28, L-MYC, and P53-shRNA (Okita et al., 2011; Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a description of the reprogramming method used, also illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: Immuno-fluorescent staining confirmed that cells in each clone were >95% positive for pluripotency markers Nanog, OCT3/4, TRA-1–60, and TRA-2–49.
source: Immuno-fluorescent staining for four pluripotency markers Nanog, OCT3/4 (also known as POU5F1), TRA-1–60, and TRA-2–49 confirmed that cells in each clone were >95% positive for each marker [Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–F].
evidence: This is a quality control result from immunofluorescence analysis, also shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: hiPSC pluripotency was verified by directed differentiation of the clones into endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm lineages.
source: hiPSC pluripotency was further verified by directed differentiation of the clones into endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm lineages, and by assessing changes in pluripotency and lineage marker expression specific to the three germ layers [Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1G].
evidence: This is a quality control result from differentiation experiments, also shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: All clones were confirmed to be diploid.
source: All clones were confirmed to be diploid, and, with the exception of two sets of clones from related donors, all clones were unrelated to each other, verifying that archived clones are unique to the respective donor and that inadvertent cross-contamination of cells from independent donors did not occur [Figure 2C].
evidence: This is a quality control result from SNP array analysis, also shown in Figure 2C.

claim: With the exception of two sets of clones from related donors, all clones were unrelated to each other.
source: All clones were confirmed to be diploid, and, with the exception of two sets of clones from related donors, all clones were unrelated to each other, verifying that archived clones are unique to the respective donor and that inadvertent cross-contamination of cells from independent donors did not occur [Figure 2C].
evidence: This is a quality control result from SNP array analysis, also shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Genetic similarity was confirmed for the two familial donors (DUP_2 and DUP_3) who were known to be mother and daughter.
source: Genetic similarity was confirmed for the two familial donors (DUP_2 and DUP_3) who were known to be mother and daughter.
evidence: This is a quality control result from SNP array analysis.

claim: SNP analysis confirmed that the SNPs proximal to the 16p11.2 CNV breakpoints were consistent with previously reported values, ranging from genomic coordinates 29.4 Mb to 32.2 Mb.
source: SNP analysis also confirmed that the SNPs proximal to the 16p11.2 CNV breakpoints were consistent with previously reported values, ranging from genomic coordinates 29.4 Mb to 32.2 Mb (Weiss et al., 2008; Jacquemont et al., 2011; Blumenthal et al., 2014; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a quality control result from SNP array analysis, compared to literature values.

claim: CNVs outside of the 16p11.2 locus exist in several patients.
source: Finally, the SNP analysis revealed that CNVs outside of the 16p11.2 locus exist in several patients; these CNVs are summarized in [Supplementary file 3].
evidence: This is a finding from SNP array analysis.

claim: 40 of the 65 clones were subjected to a monolayer dual-SMAD inhibition protocol that promotes the formation of dorsal forebrain patterned neural rosettes.
source: 40 of the 65 clones were subjected to an adaptation of a monolayer dual-SMAD inhibition protocol (Shi et al., 2012) that promotes the formation of dorsal forebrain patterned neural rosettes and a variety of neuronal and glial subtypes [Figure 3A].
evidence: This is a description of the differentiation protocol used, also illustrated in Figure 3A.

claim: Flow cytometry confirmed the rapid extinction of OCT4 expression and induction of the radial-glial marker paired box 6 (PAX6) within 7 days.
source: Flow cytometry confirmed the rapid extinction of OCT4 expression and induction of the radial-glial marker paired box 6 (PAX6) within 7 days [Figure 3—figure supplement 1A].
evidence: This is a result from flow cytometry analysis, also shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There were no subjective differences between WT and 16p11.2 CNV clones in their ability to form rosettes.
source: There were no subjective differences between WT and 16p11.2 CNV clones in their ability to form rosettes [Figure 3—figure supplement 1B].
evidence: This is an observation from the differentiation experiments, also shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In time-matched wild-type (WT) control rosettes and 16p11.2 CNV rosettes, PAX6-positive radial glia were similarly arranged in radial clusters.
source: In time-matched wild-type (WT) control rosettes and 16p11.2 CNV rosettes, PAX6-positive radial glia were similarly arranged in radial clusters [Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B].
evidence: This is an observation from immunofluorescence analysis, also shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The establishment of normal epithelial polarity was inferred by the strong apical localization of N-Cadherin (NCAD)-positive adherens junctions.
source: The establishment of normal epithelial polarity was inferred by the strong apical localization of N-Cadherin (NCAD)-positive adherens junctions [Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B].
evidence: This is an inference from immunofluorescence analysis, also shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The apical end feet of the radial glia were positive for the tight junction marker zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) as well as the PAR complex protein atypical protein kinase C zeta (aPKCζ).
source: The apical end feet of the radial glia were positive for the tight junction marker zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) as well as the PAR complex protein atypical protein kinase C zeta (aPKCζ) which is consistent with the establishment of radial glial apical-basal polarity.
evidence: This is a result from immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: Mitotic cells, indicated by phospho-histone H3 (pHH3), were found within rosettes proximal to Pericentrin labeled centrosomes which were predominantly located in the center of the rosette.
source: Additionally, mitotic cells, indicated by phospho-histone H3 (pHH3), were found within rosettes proximal to Pericentrin labeled centrosomes which were predominantly located in the center of the rosette, a localization that mimics the apical localization of mitotic cells observed in radial glia in vivo (Kriegstein and Alvarez-Buylla, 2009).
evidence: This is a result from immunofluorescence analysis, compared to in vivo observations.

claim: After 45 days of monolayer differentiation, cells exhibited characteristically long, branching neuron-specific class III β-tubulin (TUJ1) positive projections, and a small portion of young neurons was positive for neuronal nuclear protein (NEUN).
source: A subset of clones was further differentiated to assess their ability to generate immature neurons. After 45 days of monolayer differentiation, cells exhibited characteristically long, branching neuron-specific class III β-tubulin (TUJ1) positive projections, and a small portion of young neurons was positive for neuronal nuclear protein (NEUN) [Figure 3—figure supplement 1C].
evidence: This is a result from immunofluorescence analysis of differentiated neurons, also shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: All clones showed strong enrichment for anterior- and dorsal-specific markers, confirming the establishment of anterior cortical identities in culture.
source: Our initial analysis prospectively examined markers that should be enriched or depleted in neurectoderm of the dorsal telencephalon (Rubenstein et al., 1998). All clones showed strong enrichment for anterior- and dorsal-specific markers, confirming the establishment of anterior cortical identities in culture [Figure 3C].
evidence: This is a result from RNA-seq analysis of regionalization markers, also shown in Figure 3C.

claim: PCA showed strong segregation of the clones into two distinct populations that were entirely unrelated to 16p11.2 genotype.
source: Surprisingly, PCA showed strong segregation of the clones into two distinct populations that were entirely unrelated to 16p11.2 genotype [Figure 4A].
evidence: This is a result from principal components analysis of RNA-seq data, also shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Principle components 1 and 2 were associated with elevated expression of OCT3/4, which was due to the unanticipated random integration, and inappropriate expression, of episomal reprogramming vectors.
source: With further analysis, we found that principle components 1 and 2 were associated with elevated expression of OCT3/4, which was subsequently confirmed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) and quantitative real time PCR (qRT-PCR) to be due to the unanticipated random integration, and inappropriate expression, of episomal reprogramming vectors [Figure 4—figure supplement 1].
evidence: This is a finding from PCA and qPCR analysis, also shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: A novel pseudo-alignment pipeline was able to deconvolve counts for a given reprogramming gene to those generated from the genome and those generated from an integrated plasmid.
source: With a novel pseudo-alignment pipeline, we were able to deconvolve counts for a given reprogramming gene to those generated from the genome and those generated from an integrated plasmid [Figure 4B,C].
evidence: This is a description of a novel bioinformatic method developed in the study, with results shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: Integration-free hiPSC-derived NPCs express LIN28a, MYCL, and SOX2.
source: Notably, the integration-free hiPSC-derived NPCs express LIN28a, MYCL, and SOX2.
evidence: This is a finding from the pseudo-alignment analysis.

claim: Although several clones had integrated plasmids that encode LIN28a, MYCL, and SOX2, the reprogramming vectors did not significantly contribute to the abundance of the respective mRNAs.
source: Although several clones had integrated plasmids that encode each transcript, the reprogramming vectors did not significantly contribute to the abundance of the respective mRNAs [Figure 4C].
evidence: This is a finding from the pseudo-alignment analysis, also shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Approximately 10% of KLF4 transcripts detected were expressed from the plasmid.
source: Conversely, approximately 10% of KLF4 transcripts detected were expressed from the plasmid and 40% of POU5F1 (OCT3/4) transcripts were plasmid-derived.
evidence: This is a finding from the pseudo-alignment analysis.

claim: 40% of POU5F1 (OCT3/4) transcripts were plasmid-derived.
source: Conversely, approximately 10% of KLF4 transcripts detected were expressed from the plasmid and 40% of POU5F1 (OCT3/4) transcripts were plasmid-derived.
evidence: This is a finding from the pseudo-alignment analysis.

claim: A significant increase (p=0.0385) in the proportion of pHH3-positive cells was observed in the DEL Int+ differentiated NPCs affected by random integration of the POU5F1 plasmid.
source: Notably, We observed a significant increase (p=0.0385) in the proportion of pHH3-positive cells in the DEL Int+ differentiated NPCs affected by random integration of the POU5F1 plasmid [Figure 4—figure supplement 2A].
evidence: This is a finding from quantification of mitotic cells, also shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: 3612 differentially expressed (DE) genes were identified with an adjusted p-value<0.05 due to integration, of which 1739 genes (48.15%) were downregulated in integration-containing (Int+) clones relative to integration-free (Int-) clones.
source: After correcting for the effects of sex, 16p11.2 genotype, and sequencing batch [Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–E], we identified 3612 differentially expressed (DE) genes with an adjusted p-value<0.05, of which 1739 genes (48.15%) were downregulated in integration-containing (Int+) clones relative to integration-free (Int-) clones.
evidence: This is a finding from differential expression analysis.

claim: At a false detection rate (FDR) < 0.25, over 52 functions were enriched among low p-value/upregulated genes including pathways related to embryonic development and regionalization, HOX gene activation, transcription, and translation.
source: At a false detection rate (FDR) < 0.25, over 52 functions were enriched among low p-value/upregulated genes including pathways related to embryonic development and regionalization, HOX gene activation, transcription, and translation [Figure 4E].
evidence: This is a finding from GSEA analysis, also shown in Figure 4E.

claim: 355 functions were enriched among low p-value/downregulated genes including pathways related to cell death, cell adhesion, and the JAK/STAT cascade.
source: 355 functions were enriched among low p-value/downregulated genes including pathways related to cell death, cell adhesion, and the JAK/STAT cascade [Supplementary file 4].
evidence: This is a finding from GSEA analysis.

claim: The transcriptional effects of integration would confound experimentally relevant phenotypes caused by 16p11.2 CNVs, and the Int+ clones were excluded from subsequent analyses.
source: Based on these results, we concluded that the transcriptional effects of integration would confound experimentally relevant phenotypes caused by 16p11.2 CNVs, and the Int+ clones were excluded from subsequent analyses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the integration analysis that informed the study design.

claim: An insufficient number of Int- 16p11.2 duplication clones remained (n = 4) for meaningful analysis, so further studies focused exclusively on 16p11.2 deletion clones.
source: Importantly, an insufficient number of Int- 16p11.2 duplication clones remained (n = 4) for meaningful analysis, so further studies focused exclusively on 16p11.2 deletion clones.
evidence: This is a statement about the study design decision based on available samples.

claim: PCA revealed that the DEL and WT populations clustered according to genotype within the first two principal components after accounting for batch effect correction.
source: PCA revealed that the DEL and WT populations clustered according to genotype within the first two principal components after accounting for batch effect correction [Figure 5A].
evidence: This is a result from PCA analysis of Int- clones, also shown in Figure 5A.

claim: There are 56 canonical gene IDs located in the 16p11.2 locus between positions 28,800,000 and 30,400,000.
source: There are 56 canonical gene IDslocated in the 16p11.2 locus between positions 28,800,000 and 30,400,000 [Figure 5D].
evidence: This is a genomic characterization, also shown in Figure 5D.

claim: 14 of the 16p11.2 region genes were differentially expressed, and all were downregulated which is consistent with copy number-dependent effects on mRNA abundance.
source: Of these, 14 of the 16p11.2 region genes were differentially expressed, and all were downregulated which is consistent with copy number-dependent effects on mRNA abundance [Figure 5B].
evidence: This is a finding from differential expression analysis, also shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In total, 107 DE genes were identified in the DEL samples relative to WT (adjusted p-value<0.05).

claim: The differentially expressed gene list is statistically significantly enriched for genes associated with ASD, including two genes outside the 16p11.2 region (LHFPL3, CNTNAP2).

Using a linear mixed model implemented by the DuplicateCorrelations() function of limma/voom to account for shared patient identities across clones, we identified 40 genes as differentially expressed, 17 of which were in common with the genes presented in the first differential expression analysis [Figure 5—figure supplement 4A].

source: Of these, 15 showed significant association with a documented clinical phenotype and four modules had highly significant correlation to patient Age, Height Z-score, Weight Z-score, and Head Circumference Z-score.
evidence: This is a finding from WGCNA analysis.

evidence: This is a finding from GSEA analysis.

claim: Although metabolic genes represent the majority of significantly enriched pathways in this GSEA, the highest normalization scores were observed in general cellular processes and signaling pathways.
source: Although metabolic genes represent the majority of significantly enriched pathways in this GSEA, the highest normalization scores were observed in general cellular processes and signaling pathways [Figure 6C and D].
evidence: This is a finding from GSEA analysis, also shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: The pink4 module had both high significance and high correlation with key DEL clinical phenotypes.
source: Of the four modules related to body mass and language, the pink4 module had both high significance and high correlation with key DEL clinical phenotypes [Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplements 1, 2].

source: Notably, pink4 was highly positively correlated with donor Age and Weight Z-score, and negatively correlated with Height Z-score, and Head Circumference Z-Score.

source: Interestingly, it was one of the few modules significantly correlated with the Language trait and exhibits a very high magnitude of correlation.
evidence: This is a finding from WGCNA analysis.

source: The high correlation between gene module membership and significance to not only Weight_Z but also Language may unexpectedly reflect alterations in a common gene module that influence clinical features of 16p11.2 biology which have not previously been linked [Figure 6—figure supplement 3].

claim: Of the 45 genes with high membership scores for the pink4 module, several functions are potentially impacted, including components of the MAPK (FGF1) and Wnt (e.g. WIF1) signaling pathways, as well as mediators of cell growth and differentiation (e.g. AMIGO1).
source: Of the 45 genes with high membership scores for the pink4 module [Figure 6A and E], several functions are potentially impacted, including components of the MAPK (FGF1) and Wnt (e.g. WIF1) signaling pathways, as well as mediators of cell growth and differentiation (e.g. AMIGO1).

claim: The 65 hiPSC lines are a significant addition to the 14 hiPSC clones recently described by Deshpande et al., 2017.

These 65 lines are a significant addition to the 14 hiPSC clones recently described by Deshpande et al., 2017 and include donors that are age and sex matched across genotypes.

claim: 16p11.2 CNVs are implicated in a spectrum of non-CNS phenotypes, including those of the heart, kidneys, digestive tract, genitals, and bones.
source: 16p11.2 CNVs are implicated in a spectrum of non-CNS phenotypes, including those of the heart, kidneys, digestive tract, genitals, and bones (Zufferey et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Clone-to-clone variability, in part due to incomplete epigenetic remodeling and the resultant influence of epigenetic memory, may confound conclusions built upon line-to-line comparisons.
source: Clone-to-clone variability, in part due to incomplete epigenetic remodeling and the resultant influence of epigenetic memory (Polo et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2010; Lister et al., 2011), may confound conclusions built upon line-to-line comparisons (Onder and Daley, 2012).
evidence: This is a known limitation in the field supported by citations.

claim: Generating large genomic rearrangements in isogenic control lines through genetic engineering strategies such as the CRISPR/Cas9 system is technically challenging.
source: Additionally, generating large genomic rearrangements in isogenic control lines through genetic engineering strategies such as the CRISPR/Cas9 system is technically challenging (Grobarczyk et al., 2015; Tai et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a known technical limitation supported by citations.

source: We found that all 14 DE genes within the canonical 16p11.2 interval were located within a shorter interval of the chromosome where deletions overlapped for the five subjects with known breakpoints.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis in the context of known deletion intervals.

claim: Of 56 genes within and flanking the deletion intervals of the clones evaluated, 15 are expressed at or below the limits of detection.
source: Of 56 genes within and flanking the deletion intervals of the clones evaluated, 15 are expressed at or below the limits of detection.
evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq analysis.

claim: The remaining 41 genes in the 16p11.2 region are likely to have roles in early cortical development that may be affected when copy number is altered.
source: Conversely, it also stands to reason that the remaining 41 genes are likely to have roles in early cortical development that may be affected when copy number is altered.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression data.

claim: 14 genes in the 16p11.2 region are differentially expressed and all are downregulated in DEL: MAZ, DOC2A, PRRT2, PAGR1, TAOK2, KIF22, HIRIP3, ALDOA, C16orf92, INO80E, MAPK3, KCTD13, SEZ6L2, and FAM57B.
source: Of these, 14 are differentially expressed and all are downregulated in DEL: MAZ, DOC2A, PRRT2, PAGR1, TAOK2, KIF22, HIRIP3, ALDOA, C16orf92, INO80E, MAPK3, KCTD13, SEZ6L2, and FAM57B.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: The statistically significant downregulation of 14 genes suggests that these 16p11.2 loci are worthy of increased scrutiny as genes that may commonly influence developmental outcomes across individuals that share this deletion interval.
source: Their statistically significant downregulation suggests that these 16p11.2 loci are worthy of increased scrutiny as genes that may commonly influence developmental outcomes across individuals that share this deletion interval.

claim: The 16p11.2 region gene MAPK3 is of particular note, as its protein product Erk1 is known to interact with several other observed DE genes (e.g. SELE, CALML6, RAF1, SEMA4A).
source: Of particular note is the 16p11.2 region gene MAPK3, as its protein product Erk1 is known to interact with several other observed DE genes (e.g. SELE, CALML6, RAF1, SEMA4A).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differential expression findings in the context of known protein interactions.

claim: The finding that MAPK3 is downregulated supports existing work suggesting that the Erk1 MAPK pathway may drive phenotypic abnormalities associated with the 16p11.2 CNV.
source: This finding supports existing work suggesting that the Erk1 MAPK pathway may drive phenotypic abnormalities associated with the 16p11.2 CNV (Pucilowska et al., 2018; Pucilowska et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the context of prior research.

claim: No changes in NPC proliferation were observed between wild type and deletion lines, indicating that MAPK3 may not influence NPC proliferation in these 16p11.2 patient lines.
source: Although we detected a decrease in MAPK3 gene expression in all the 16p11.2 deletion lines [Figure 5—figure supplement 1A], we did not observe any changes in NPC proliferation between wild type and deletion lines indicating that MAPK3 may not influence NPC proliferation in these 16p11.2 patient lines [Figure 4—figure supplement 2A].
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays, also shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The finding of no change in NPC proliferation is consistent with prior work that also found no significant difference in the proliferation of DEL cells at the NPC stage.
source: This is consistent with prior work that also found no significant difference in the proliferation of DEL cells at the NPC stage (Deshpande et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior research findings.

claim: In addition to the 14 DE genes within the 16p11.2 locus, there are 93 additional genes that are differentially expressed.
source: In addition to the 14 DE genes within the 16p11.2 locus, there are 93 additional genes that are differentially expressed.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Fifteen of the differentially expressed genes are identified as being generally related to psychiatric disease, and nine are more specifically identified as related to ASD.
source: Fifteen of these genes are identified as being generally related to psychiatric disease, and nine are more specifically identified as related to ASD [Figure 5—figure supplement 3A].
evidence: This is a finding from gene enrichment analysis, also shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A.

claim: All the ASD-related genes are listed in the SFARI Gene Scoring Module database and are associated with at least five published reports supporting their role as a candidate gene in ASD.
source: All these genes are listed in the SFARI Gene Scoring Module database (Abrahams et al., 2013) and are associated with at least five published reports supporting their role as a candidate gene in ASD.
evidence: This is a characterization of the ASD-related genes based on a database.

claim: CNTNAP2, a neurexin family member that is important for excitatory synapse formation and function, is one of the strongest known candidate-genes for ASD risk.
source: Of these genes, CNTNAP2, a neurexin family member that is important excitatory synapse formation and function, is one of the strongest known candidate-genes for ASD risk (Abrahams et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a characterization of CNTNAP2 based on prior knowledge.

claim: Several additional DE genes are also relevant to excitatory synapses in mature neurons (e.g. PRRT2, CALML6, C1QL3, DOC2A, GABRE, C1QL3, CNTNAP2).
source: Several additional DE genes are also relevant to excitatory synapses in mature neurons (e.g. PRRT2, CALML6, C1QL3, DOC2A, GABRE, C1QL3, CNTNAP2), and may reflect early perturbations in gene networks relevant to cortical excitatory networks.
evidence: This is a characterization of DE genes based on their known functions.

claim: Previous work reports changes in neurite branching and synapse development in more mature neurons.
source: Previous work reports changes in neurite branching and synapse development in more mature neurons (Deshpande et al., 2017), and here, we find genes that may be related to these later changes are differentially expressed well before such neurons emerge in culture.
evidence: This is a comparison to prior research findings.

claim: Genes that may be related to later changes in neurite branching and synapse development are differentially expressed well before such neurons emerge in culture.
source: Previous work reports changes in neurite branching and synapse development in more mature neurons (Deshpande et al., 2017), and here, we find genes that may be related to these later changes are differentially expressed well before such neurons emerge in culture.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differential expression findings in the context of prior research.

claim: The 16p11.2 region gene KCTD13 is important for the maintenance of synaptic transmission in the CA1 region of the hippocampus, with its loss resulting in decreased fEPSP slope and the frequency of mEPSP currents.
source: For example, the 16p11.2 region gene KCTD13 is important for the maintenance of synaptic transmission in the CA1 region of the hippocampus, with its loss resulting in decreased fEPSP slope and the frequency of mEPSP currents (Escamilla et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a characterization of KCTD13 based on prior research.

source: Interestingly, the 16p11.2 region gene TAOK2 has been shown to influence the differentiation, basal dendrite formation, and axonal projection of pyramidal neurons in the cortex with its deletion resulting in abnormal dendrite formation and impaired axonal elongation in mouse brains (de Anda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a characterization of TAOK2 based on prior research.

claim: The expression of KCTD13 and TAOK2 was found to be reduced across all deletion lines.
source: We found the expression of KCTD13 and TAOK2 to be reduced across all deletion lines suggesting that reduced KCTD13 and TAOK2 expression in cortical progenitors may impact cortical network development and the maintenance of appropriate synaptic tone in the cortex of autistic individuals.

claim: Reduced KCTD13 and TAOK2 expression in cortical progenitors may impact cortical network development and the maintenance of appropriate synaptic tone in the cortex of autistic individuals.
source: We found the expression of KCTD13 and TAOK2 to be reduced across all deletion lines suggesting that reduced KCTD13 and TAOK2 expression in cortical progenitors may impact cortical network development and the maintenance of appropriate synaptic tone in the cortex of autistic individuals.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the differential expression findings.

claim: The DE gene list includes features that may predict alterations related to movement or locomotion of the cell.
source: Other features that the DE gene list may predict include alterations related to movement or locomotion of the cell [Figure 5G].
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DE gene list, also shown in Figure 5G.

source: Several DE genes modulate actin and cytoskeletal organization, which could contribute to abnormal cell morphology (e.g. SELE, TEKT4, TUBGCP4, KLHL4).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DE gene list based on known gene functions.

claim: Three downregulated genes are related to glucose metabolism and glycogen synthesis (e.g. TLCD3B, FBP2, ALDOA), suggesting that changes in cellular metabolism and energy management may influence outcomes.
source: Additionally, three downregulated genes are related to glucose metabolism and glycogen synthesis (e.g. TLCD3B, FBP2, ALDOA), suggesting that changes in cellular metabolism and energy management may influence outcomes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DE gene list based on known gene functions.

source: miR-6723 itself is enriched in neurons relative to microglia, astrocytes, and endothelial cells (Spaethling et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a characterization of miR-6723 based on prior research.

source: Interestingly, it is also downregulated in term placentas of women with chronic Chagas disease, suggesting a role in cellular proliferation or immune response (Winn et al., 2007; Juiz et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a characterization of miR-6723 based on prior research.

claim: Four other miRNAs appear in the differential expression gene list and have roles in proliferation that may impact progenitor function.
source: Four other miRNAs appear in the differential expression gene list and have roles in proliferation that may impact progenitor function.
evidence: This is a characterization of DE miRNAs based on known functions.

claim: miR-301B impairs cellular senescence and has a role in the spread of certain cancers.
source: Of note, miR-301B impairs cellular senescence and has a role in the spread of certain cancers (Ramalho-Carvalho et al., 2017; Danesh et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a characterization of miR-301B based on prior research.

claim: miR-637 inhibits tumorigenesis, and its downregulation may enhance cell proliferation.
source: miR-637 inhibits tumorigenesis, and its downregulation may enhance cell proliferation (Zhang et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a characterization of miR-637 based on prior research.

source: It is also worth noting that SNP array data show that 4 of the 13 DEL Int- clones contained additional CNVs, including microdeletion in 14q11.1, a microduplication in 14q11.2, and a microdeletion in 7p11.2.

source: All of these CNVs are potentially associated with neurodevelopmental abnormalities (Zahir et al., 2007; Varvagiannis et al., 2014), and it is possible that these additional CNVs contribute to the transcriptional alterations.

source: However, there is no significant difference in the average fold change of DE gene expression in DEL relative to WT between the subset of clones carrying these additional CNVs and the remaining DEL clones [Figure 5—figure supplement 1B].

claim: The additional CNVs are unlikely to account for the transcriptional changes in the NPCs reported.
source: Although it is important to document all background CNVs for future reference, these CNVs are unlikely to account for the transcriptional changes in the NPCs reported here.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of clones with additional CNVs.

claim: Patient-specific transcriptional abnormalities, in addition to a core 16p11.2 transcript deficiency, may interact to generate a heterogeneous patient phenotype.
source: This work also suggests that patient-specific transcriptional abnormalities, in addition to a core 16p11.2 transcript deficiency, may interact to generate a heterogeneous patient phenotype.

source: Our WGCNA analysis identified several modules correlated with phenotypes within 16p11.2 deletion patients [Figure 6A].
evidence: This is a finding from WGCNA analysis, also shown in Figure 6A.

source: Interestingly, these signals were related not only to higher order neurological functions, but to physical attributes and body plan.

source: These modules do not contain genes identified as distinguishing DEL from WT samples.

source: The grey module also contained the most DE genes (n = 32) in the DE pipeline presented in Figure 5 and genes identified in the linear mixed model pipeline (n = 16) [Figure 5—figure supplement 4].

claim: It is possible that the gene programs accounting for phenotype heterogeneity within DEL are due to transcriptional programs that exist independent of the 16p11.2 deletion region.
source: However, it is possible that the gene programs accounting for phenotype heterogeneity within DEL are due to transcriptional programs that exist independent of the 16p11.2 deletion region.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the WGCNA findings.

claim: Patient-specific etiology may be due to an interaction of a generalized existing liability posed by the presence of the 16p11.2 deletion interacting with patient-specific features.
source: This further reinforces the possibility that patient-specific etiology may be due to an interaction of a generalized existing liability posed by the presence of the 16p11.2 deletion interacting with patient-specific features.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the WGCNA findings.

claim: Within the four modules most highly correlated with a spectrum of patient traits, the member genes were most often significantly associated with metabolic functions.
source: Within the four modules most highly correlated with a spectrum of patient traits, the member genes were most often significantly associated with metabolic functions [Figure 6C].
evidence: This is a finding from GSEA analysis of WGCNA modules, also shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The strongest enrichments in the four modules fell within a select set of functions related to cell responses to external stimuli.
source: However, the strongest enrichments fell within a select set of functions related to cell responses to external stimuli [Figure 6D].
evidence: This is a finding from GSEA analysis of WGCNA modules, also shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Patient phenotypic variance might account for heterogeneous clinical presentation, and this variance might emerge both in metabolic and signaling functions of the cell.
source: This supports the hypothesis that patient phenotypic variance might account for heterogeneous clinical presentation, and that this variance might emerge both in metabolic and signaling functions of the cell.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GSEA findings.

claim: The greater enrichment of cell-cell signaling pathways suggest that the phenotype might extend beyond simple metabolic dysfunction and include a breakdown of intercellular communication systems tightly linked to growth and metabolism of the cell.
source: However, the greater enrichment of cell-cell signaling pathways suggest that the phenotype might extend beyond simple metabolic dysfunction and include a breakdown of intercellular communication systems tightly linked to growth and metabolism of the cell.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GSEA findings.

claim: The genes most highly associated with the pink4 module contain regulators of major developmental cascades in development that could conceivably disrupt gene programs related to both nervous system function and general cellular growth, including Wnt pathway negative regulator WIF1, and Erk1/2 MAPK pathway effector FGF1.
source: The genes most highly associated with this module contain regulators of major developmental cascades in development that could conceivably disrupt gene programs related to both nervous system function and general cellular growth, including Wnt pathway negative regulator WIF1, and Erk1/2 MAPK pathway effector FGF1 [Figure 6E].
evidence: This is a characterization of genes in the pink4 module, also shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Increased Weight Z-score in the patient cohort was associated with reduced expression of insulin (INS), but increased expression of fetal growth-regulating insulin-like growth factor 2.
source: Interestingly, increased Weight Z-score in this patient cohort was associated with reduced expression of insulin (INS), but increased expression of fetal growth-regulating insulin-like growth factor 2.
evidence: This is a finding from the WGCNA analysis.

claim: If generalized insulin-related signaling abnormalities exist in these patients, this disruption would likely be compounded by established alterations in MAPK signaling, an insulin signaling effector mediating cell growth, leading to a high BMI phenotype.
source: Although the present study characterizes neural tissue, if generalized insulin-related signaling abnormalities exist in these patients, this disruption would likely be compounded by established alterations in MAPK signaling, an insulin signaling effector mediating cell growth, leading to a high BMI phenotype.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: The identification of BMI-associated genes within NPCs could be attributable to the fact that some aspects of the gene program modulated by 16p11.2 deletion may represent a generalized phenotype with tissue type-specific effects.
source: Taken together with the observation made about the larger four-module block, the identification of BMI-associated genes within NPCs could be attributable to the fact that some aspects of the gene program modulated by 16p11.2 deletion may represent a generalized phenotype with tissue type-specific effects.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the WGCNA findings.

claim: The association of the pink4 module with Head Circumference Z-score suggests a possible link with abnormal activity within NPCs, as head circumference has been associated with aberrant proliferation in NPCs, and DEL patients have been observed to have decreased head circumference.
source: The pink4 module is similarly associated with two functions that could be conceivably impacted by dysregulation of the developing brain. One of these changes, Head Circumference Z-score, suggests a possible link with abnormal activity within NPCs, as head circumference has been associated with aberrant proliferation in NPCs, and DEL patients have been observed to have decreased head circumference (Qureshi et al., 2014; Vaccarino et al., 2009).

claim: The association of the pink4 module with language deficits suggest a possible link to more mature circuit assembly and function, coincident with previous reports of language disruption associated within the 16p11.2 deletion phenotype.
source: Additionally, the association of this module with language deficits suggest a possible link to more mature circuit assembly and function, coincident with previous reports of language disruption associated within the 16p11.2 deletion phenotype (Blackmon et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the WGCNA findings in the context of prior research.

claim: The correlation between sets of genes in the pink4 module and phenotypes associated with abnormal neurodevelopment invites speculation into the heterogeneous nature of language deficits in patients with 16p11.2 CNVs.
source: Together, the correlation between these sets of genes and phenotypes associated with abnormal neurodevelopment invites speculation into the heterogeneous nature of language deficits in patients with 16p11.2 CNVs.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the WGCNA findings.

claim: The observed relationship between trait and expression of specific genes (e.g. Weight Z-score and INS expression) indicate that the combined correlations are not entirely attributable to normal changes in weight with age.
source: While it is not possible to pinpoint what aspects of the genetic signature might be attributable to this association, the observed relationship between trait and expression of specific genes (e.g. Weight Z-score and INS expression) indicate that the combined correlations are not entirely attributable to normal changes in weight with age.

claim: The results of the WGCNA analysis suggest that several gene modules may be associated with a spectrum of clinical outcomes with 16p11.2 microdeletion.
source: The results of the WGCNA analysis suggest, as a whole, that several gene modules may be associated with a spectrum of clinical outcomes with 16p11.2 microdeletion, that some BMI-associated changes are detected even in a cell type presumably unrelated to BMI (neural progenitors), and that some of these correlations with clinical features involve genes outside of the 16p11.2 microdeletion.

claim: Some BMI-associated changes are detected even in a cell type presumably unrelated to BMI (neural progenitors).
source: The results of the WGCNA analysis suggest, as a whole, that several gene modules may be associated with a spectrum of clinical outcomes with 16p11.2 microdeletion, that some BMI-associated changes are detected even in a cell type presumably unrelated to BMI (neural progenitors), and that some of these correlations with clinical features involve genes outside of the 16p11.2 microdeletion.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the WGCNA findings.

claim: Some correlations with clinical features involve genes outside of the 16p11.2 microdeletion.
source: The results of the WGCNA analysis suggest, as a whole, that several gene modules may be associated with a spectrum of clinical outcomes with 16p11.2 microdeletion, that some BMI-associated changes are detected even in a cell type presumably unrelated to BMI (neural progenitors), and that some of these correlations with clinical features involve genes outside of the 16p11.2 microdeletion.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the WGCNA findings.

claim: It is important to screen clones for cryptically integrated reprogramming plasmids, especially as published methods highlight the lack of integration when using episomal reprogramming vectors.
source: Finally, we emphasize the importance of screening clones for cryptically integrated reprogramming plasmids, especially as published methods highlight the lack of integration when using episomal reprogramming vectors.
